title: Lightweight eval field notes: human-in-loop probes & quickbench sketch
body:
Purpose / context:
Quick personal notes for a lightweight evaluation workflow we can run weekly on hosted models and new quantized variants. Goal is a cheap, fast smoke-test for regressions in: recall on short factual prompts, instruction following, and context-stitching when KV cache is cold. This is NOT a replacement for full eval bench — it is a fast guardrail for deployment rollouts and model swaps.

High level idea:
- Keep test ~200 prompts, split across micro-suites: factuals (50), instructions (70), continuity/chaining (40), hallucination-sensitive (40).
- Human-in-the-loop triage: produce top-3 outputs, send a short sampler (10 examples per suite) to 2 reviewers for quick thumbs-up/down and a one-line reason. Average triage time target: <15m per reviewer.
- Automated metrics: exact match / edit distance for factuals; instruction score (binary pass if follow step counts); next-turn continuity loss (token-level perplexity proxy); hallucination detector score (lexical overlap with retrieved evidence).

Paper/blogs skimmed and quick takeaways:
1) "Lightweight model evaluation at scale" (arXiv 2024) — argues for stratified micro-suites and human adjudication on edge cases. Takeaway: sampling strategy matters more than absolute size; include adversarial seeds derived from production logs.
2) "Prompt-sensitive hallucination probes" (blog) — simple retrieval-based reference helps build a binary hallucination signal. Implement a cheap BM25 retrieval over our public knowledge base for the probe harness.
3) "KV cache warmup and early tokens" (conference talk notes) — observed that short warmup sequences cause non-linear degradation in Answer-F1 for low-bit models. Add dedicated cold-cache suite.

Measurement plan (prototype):
- Build Quickbench harness: yaml config per micro-suite, generator scripts to mutate prompts (paraphrase, shorten, noise injection), and a runner that hits hosted API + quantized local variants.
- Output: csv with per-example outputs, token counts, latency p50/p95, and metric columns. Also keep small html summary for reviewers with 10-shot example grids.
- Daily cron job produces baseline against the "canary" model. If any metric delta > threshold (factual EM drop >5 pp, instruction pass drop >8 pp, hallucination rate +6 pp), trigger triage run.

Open questions / design tradeoffs:
- How to pick 200 prompts without dataset bias? Idea: 60% synthetic seeds + 40% sampled from anonymized production traces (need privacy check with Privacy team).
- Reviewer workflow: integrate triage into Redwood Console? Quick hack: use a Google Form summary for reviewers first, then integrate with console later.
- Cost math: aim for < $10 per daily run on hosted API — approximate token budget and batching required.

Short experiment notes (what I ran locally):
- Ran 50-fact micro-suite against local quant-8 model and hosted base on 2026-06-20. Observed EM delta ~3.2 pp; latency p95 for quantized was ~1.8x but token cost 0.45x.
- Cold-cache suite: saw multiple context drops for long-chained questions (drop ~10% instruction pass). Possible mitigation: pre-prime with a short context warmup token or prefetch KV shards.

Immediate next steps (for this week):
1) Build generator scripts for the 4 micro-suites (Sanjay) — baseline skeleton done, needs paraphrase heuristics.
2) Quick HTML reporter that collates top-3 outputs and inline reviewer form (Lena) — ask UX for minimal layout.
3) Privacy check on sampling production traces and write a short policy note for legal (Fenna).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a small section on thresholds and escalation routing in rollouts doc (link later).
- Prototype BM25 retrieval against public KB (fast, can be shipped as a local dependency).
- Explore cheap hallucination classifier (binary) using logistic on lexical overlap + entailment signal.

Riff ideas (longer-term):
- Continuous curator: identify prompt families that fluctuate most across model versions and keep those in a "watchlist". Could feed back into training or prompt design.
- Micro-A/B in console: lightweight canary that runs only on 5% of traffic and flags if quickbench metrics diverge.

Slack notes / references: pulled examples from #prod-logs-sample and asked initial thoughts in #eng-applied-ml on 2026-06-22. Will paste console links once reporter is up.

If anyone reading this and willing to help: comment inline or ping me. Want to run the first daily harness by Friday (2026-06-25).
